newsitem.title: USA: Warner gets FDA approval for FemPatch.
newsitem.headline: Warner gets FDA approval for FemPatch.

text.p: Warner-Lambert Co's Parke-Davis Inc unit said it received U.S. regulatory approval to market FemPatch, a low-dose transdermal estrogen patch for the treatment of menopausal symptoms.
FemPatch was co-developed by Parke-Davis, a division of Warner-Lambert, and Cygnus Inc, which will manufacture the product.
The product uses a low, 0.025 mg dose of 17 beta-estradiol, a natural form of estrogen, in a thin, once-weekly patch.
Transdermal estrogen replacement systems currently on the market all contain the ingredient 17 beta-estradiol in doses ranging from 0.0375 mg to 0.1 mg.

Parke-Davis said FemPatch treats moderate to severe vasomotor menopausal symptoms using a patented matrix system that delivers estradiol through the skin in a consistent, low dose, reaching maximum blood levels within 24 hours and then maintaining constant blood levels for seven days.
